I came in with an urgent yet simple-to-resolve medical issue: prepared with a recent and relevant prescription from my previous doctor for critical daily thyroid medication, I needed a rewrite from any GP in Swansea.
I clearly communicated to Dr. Carly Smith that I had already been without one of my two vital medications for over a week. Despite her awareness that these are essential for someone without a thyroid, it came as a surprise that she refused to prescribe the second medication simply because she was unfamiliar with it, stating that she was 'under no obligation' to do so.
It is deeply concerning—and frankly unacceptable—for a doctor to take such a heedless stance when faced with a patient in need. This medical establishment, with its team of a few other GPs, should be approached with caution. Thankfully, a second opinion at another GP resulted in the prescription being issued without problem—contrary to Dr. Carly’s advisement—proving that the medication was readily available at local pharmacies. By any means, being redirected for such a simple medical assessment is not only unnecessary but also entirely inconsiderate of the patient’s well-being, time, medical needs, and individual circumstances.
Dr. Carly’s impatience, negligence, and haughty demeanor while handling such a simple prescription, despite the ample resources to familiarize herself with it, will surely leave a lasting impression on me as a young hypothyroid
